During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in the Petition and prayed for the adoption of tariff and submitted that there had been a delay in obtaining consent from the buyers, and there was an 16. The Petitioner was directed to submit the reasons for delay in approaching the Commission for the adoption of tariff as per the Guidelines, status of communications with the MNRE in this regard, and to file the status of the PPA/PSA for entire capacity allocated to the bidders who participated in the e-Reverse Auction. 18. The Petitioner in response to the Commission’s query related to delay in approaching the Commission for the adoption of tariff has submitted that, as per clause 11.4 of the Guidelines dated 09.06.2023, NHPC was required to file the Petition for the adoption of tariff within 15 days of e-Reverse Auction i.e. by 08.03.2024. However, the instant Petition has been filed on 20.12.2024. The Petitioner has submitted that there is delay in obtaining consent from the buyers, since DISCOM(s) take considerable time in evaluation of the prices of various tenders floated by REIAs. Therefore, a request letter dated 25.05.2024 was made to the MNRE, GOI to review the provision of Clause 11.4 of the Guidelines dated 09.06.2023 and period of 60 days after signing of the PPA/PSA may be allowed for approaching the Commission for the adoption of tariff. However, till the date of filing of the present Petition, no clarification was issued by the MNRE. information/ clarification in compliance with the direction of the Commission vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 19.02.2025. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission deemed it appropriate to permit all the Respondents, as a last opportunity, to file their respective replies. Learned counsel for Respondent No.3, BN Hybrid Power-1 Private Limited, prayed for time to file a reply in the matter, if required. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission deemed it appropriate to provide all the Respondents, a last opportunity, to file their respective replies and accordingly order in the matter was reserved. - xix) _Dispute resolution is subject to the Appropriate Commission, CERC, or SERC/JERC. If difficulties arise in giving effect to any provision of these Guidelines or interpretation of the Guidelines, the Ministry of Power is empowered to do so with the approval of the Minister, New & Renewable Energy. Renewable energy components, including Energy Storage System (ESS) components charged with RE sources, are eligible for RPO compliance._ 31. For the execution of the project, the Petitioner constituted a Tender Evaluation Committee, which was further re-constituted, comprising of the following: - _10.0 All disputes arising out of and/or in connection with the selection of ISTS-Connected ‘firm & dispatchable’ RE Power Projects coupled with energy storage system under the said RfS and execution of PPA thereto shall be governed by laws of India and shall be subject to the jurisdiction of Courts of Faridabad._ of the RfS. We observe that the Petitioner has submitted that all the conditions as per the RfS documents have been compiled with from issue of NIT till date. The Petitioner has further submitted that there is no deviation made in the bid documents from the provisions of the FDRE Guidelines and this has been certified by the Petitioner through the confirmation certificates i.e. CONFORMITY CERTIFICATE (Bid Evaluation in conformity with provision of the RfS) and CERTIFICATE (No deviation certificate in RfS w.r.t Bidding guidelines) both dated 16.09.2024. The relevant extract of the said conformity certificates dated 16.09.2024 is as under: _competitive bidding process conducted in accordance with these Guidelines.”_ In the present case, the e-RA was concluded on 22.02.2024, and accordingly, the Petitioner was required to approach the Commission for the adoption of tariff by 08.03.2024. However, the Petitioner, NHPC, filed the present Petition only on 20.12.2024 (e-filing portal). Accordingly, vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 19.02.2025, the Petitioner was directed to indicate the reasons for the delay in approaching the Commission as per Clause 11.4 of the Solar Guidelines. In response, the Petitioner has submitted that this Commission, in previous cases, had directed the Petitioner to only seek adoption of tariff once capacity is tied up and the PPAs and PSAs for that capacity have been executed, and in the present case, although NHPC had offered the entire capacity to UPPCL after the conclusion of e-RA and the identification of the successful bidders, neither PPAs with the bidders had been executed nor had the Petitioner received UPPCL’s consent for execution of the PSA. NHPC has submitted that immediately after UPPCL accepted and consented to its offer on 27.11.2024; the Petitioner filed the present Petition for the adoption of tariff on 20.12.2024, anticipating execution of the PPAs and PSA at a later stage. We have considered the justification provided by NHPC for delay in approaching the Commission for the adoption in tariff in terms of Clause 10.4 of the Solar Guidelines and accordingly, we condone the delay in approaching the Commission by the Petitioner. Keeping in view that, unlike the previous Solar Guidelines of 2017, the Solar Guidelines of 2023 specifically provide a timeline for distribution licensee or intermediary procurers to approach the Appropriate Commission for the adoption of tariff, we expect the Petitioner to strictly adhere to the said timelines in future.
